topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and establishes its learning objectives.

topics.label: Mutations and the cellular origins of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations can give rise to cancer through clonal evolution within a permissive biological context.

topics.label: Environmental contributions to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the contribution of environmental exposures to cancer risk and the evidence for distinguishing that contribution from chance and inherited predisposition.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed example of infection-dependent carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Environmental mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how environmental exposures produce DNA damage that can become cancer-causing mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how tumour-promoting conditions enable initiated cells to grow into cancers rather than simply causing mutations themselves.

topics.label: Biological context and carcinogen susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how susceptibility depends on the biological context of exposure and conclude with a recap of carcinogenic mechanisms and specificity.

topics.label: Evidence and methods for assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence and methodological limitations involved in linking exposures to cancer.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and placing cancer risks within everyday risk–benefit decisions.
